Downard · 1862

The Downard Journey to Utah

Documented

In the passenger register, George appears as Dowrard, a 40-year-old painter from England. The William Tapscott sailed from Liverpool on May 14 and reached New York on June 25, 1862. Sarah and several children appear in the same register.

The family research places them with the Horton D. Haight Company. That company left Florence, Nebraska, on August 10 and reached Salt Lake City on October 19. The family account reports that infant Edward died during the journey. The ship transcription’s infant entry reads Edmund, so the two records should be compared before the identification is settled.

The Spring City preservation inventory places George in town after immigration and associates him with carpentry and house painting.

People George Downard, Sarah Ann Downard, Edward Hiram Downard

Places Deptford, England, Florence, Nebraska, Spring City, Utah

Sources · George Dowrard on the William Tapscott · William Tapscott voyage · Horton D. Haight Company · Family research brief

Downard · Circa 1875–1882

The House George Built

Documented

At 109 South 200 East in Spring City, the preservation inventory identifies a two-story house of oolitic limestone. Its hall-parlor form belongs to the town’s vernacular building tradition.

The inventory dates the house to around 1875 and describes its completion in the late 1870s. It records the sale to George’s son Joseph in 1882. The property entry separates the approximate construction date from the reported transfer.

People George Downard, Joseph Downard

Places Spring City, Utah

Sources · George Downard House · Spring City Historic District registration

Downard · Early twentieth century · reports undated

John Louis Downard and the Ranches of Eastern Utah

Research in progress

Three newspaper excerpts describe a ranch sale near Woodside, a move to Nine Mile, and proposed negotiations with Wade Harness. The excerpts survive without enough issue information to put them in sequence or identify the railroad section bosses named in the ranch report.

A separate abstract records a $3,600 warranty deed from W. M. Harness to J. L. Downard. The county and meridian are missing. The Burt and Wilson abstracts are listed separately because the shared section number leaves the parcels’ relationship unresolved.

People John Louis Downard

Places Woodside, Utah, Nine Mile Canyon, Harper, Utah

Sources · Woodside ranch sale report · John Downard’s move to Nine Mile · Bluebell report on proposed property negotiations · Harness to Downard warranty deed abstract · Downard to Burt and Wilson to Harness deed abstracts

Downard · 1880–early 1920s

Minnie Thompson: From Nine Mile to Rochester

Research in progress

Minnie’s obituary places her birth in Elko County in 1880. It describes a move to Nine Mile when she was about six and records six children from her first marriage. A 1915 license notice names Minnie E. Rogers and John L. Downard as Harper residents.

The obituary reports that after months of illness she traveled to Rochester, Minnesota, for surgery for goiter. It describes complications and her return to Price, where she died at home. A separate report names Mayo Hospital. Her funeral was reported at the Price LDS Tabernacle and her burial at Price City Cemetery.

The supplied issue reference reads August 18. The year and exact death date remain open.

People Minnie Estelle Thompson Rogers Downard, John Louis Downard

Places Elko County, Nevada, Nine Mile Canyon, Harper, Utah, Rochester, Minnesota, Price, Utah

Sources · Death of Minnie Downard · John L. Downard and Minnie E. Rogers marriage-license notice · Report naming Mayo Hospital

Lambson · June 1942

A Wedding in 1942

Conflicting

The supplied summary of Bride-Elect Complimented describes a gathering at Mrs. T. A. Pedersen’s home, co-hosted by Mrs. Joseph Timothy. It records about 39 guests, a prize won by Mrs. Walter Downard, and a blue-and-green seersucker suit for the wedding.

The family record dates the marriage to June 26. The newspaper summary reports June 30 and identifies Bishop John A. Harter as officiant. The marriage return and the original newspaper issue are needed to resolve the difference and confirm the host’s identity.

People Norma Lucille Lambson, Thomas John Downard, Clace Sabey

Places Salt Lake City, Utah

Sources · Existing Lambson family archive · Bride-Elect Complimented

Freestone · World War II and after

Tom Freestone: From Prisoner of War to a Lifetime of Service

Research in progress

Tom’s obituary, as summarized in the family research, describes a wounded B-17 gunner taken prisoner after his aircraft was shot down near Vienna. The loss date, crew, turret assignment, mission count, award and march details need military documentation.

After the war the family records describe ranching around Little Brush Creek, local archaeological and preservation work, and community education. The county history reportedly records Tom’s 1964 appointment to direct juvenile court services for five counties and his work as a referee and judge pro tempore.

People Clyde Thomas Freestone

Places Vienna, Austria, Vernal, Utah, Little Brush Creek, Utah

Sources · Clyde Thomas Freestone obituary · A History of Uintah County: Scratching the Surface · Family research brief

Peterson · Late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries

The Peterson Family’s Journey from Sweden

Conflicting

The family records preserve both Pettersson and Peterson for Hilmer. A 1959 letter recalls his arrival as a boy and a stay with the Anderson family before his parents arrived. Other family accounts suggest a later arrival. Swedish parish records, census entries and passenger lists remain research targets.

The family tree connects the Peterson and Freestone branches through Maurine’s marriage to Tom Freestone in 1947.

People Johannes Gustaf Pettersson, Ericka Munter, Erik Hilmer Pettersson, Mary Alvey, Maurine Peterson

Places Sweden
